_comment: No thermal/HVAC loads here -- that stays buem's job. `lighting`/`general_appliances` hourly weekday/weekend weight arrays are Ahmed, Akhondzada, Kurnitski & Olesen (2017, Sustainable Cities and Society 35:134-144) Table 8 and Table 7 'Hospital' columns respectively (same source as schedule.json's occupancy curve). Used here as `probabilistic_event` per-hour firing-probability arrays with `gate: "none"` (schedule-driven, not occupancy-gated -- matching Ahmed et al.'s own always-on-a-schedule treatment of these loads, distinct from every other type's equipment in this package, which gates on presence/activity); `expected_probabilistic_event`'s E[power] = standby + probability * (rated - standby) formula then reproduces their intended continuous-usage-rate semantics in expectation, with `standby_power_kw: 0.0` so any given hour is stochastically either fully off or fully on rather than a smooth blend (same simplification as every other item in this file). `diagnostic_monitoring_equipment` and `kitchen` have no Ahmed et al. equivalent (that source doesn't split equipment by department) -- illustrative additions: the former scales up `clinic`'s own `medical_equipment` item for continuous 24/7 diagnostic/monitoring-gear draw (informed loosely by an AI-summarized synthesis of ASHRAE 90.1/Fundamentals-style equipment-power-density figures for hospital departments, cross-checked only for plausible order of magnitude, not independently verified against the primary standard text); the latter reflects the real kitchen this repo's Dobosi, Tanasa, Kaba, Retezan & Mihaila (2019, E3S Web of Conferences 111, 06073) case-study hospital lists in its basement floor plan (Table 1), meal-prep-weighted around breakfast/lunch/dinner service. Illustrative power ratings throughout, not calibrated against real hospital metering.
